note: Curated catalog of the standard offensive toolbox. DATA ONLY — this file executes nothing. Every invocation here is a TEMPLATE the planner draws on so proposed commands are well-formed and consistent; each one still goes through the same gated executor (approve-each, heuristic red-confirm, target/scope lock, argv-only). Templates are written from each tool's own documentation and standard usage. Placeholders use <angle-brackets>; <target> is filled by the composer's substitute_target so a rendered command points at the real engagement target and nothing else.

placeholders.<target>: Host, IP or URL under test — filled from the engagement target.
placeholders.<hashfile>: Path to a file of captured hashes.
placeholders.<binary>: Path to a local binary under analysis.
placeholders.<size>: A response size in bytes, used to filter baseline/404 noise.
placeholders.<technique>: A technique/tag name the tool understands (e.g. a nuclei tag).
placeholders.<database>: Database name on the target DBMS.
placeholders.<pattern>: A literal string or regex to search for.

tools.name: nmap
tools.purpose: Port, service and version discovery, plus a large scripting engine for protocol-level enumeration. The default first look at a host.

templates.label: Full TCP port sweep
templates.note: Find every open TCP port first; enumerate them in a second pass.

templates.label: Service + default scripts on known ports
templates.note: Run after the sweep, against only the ports it found.

templates.label: Top UDP ports
templates.note: UDP is slow; the top ports catch SNMP/DNS/NTP/TFTP.

templates.label: Vulnerability-ish NSE sweep
templates.note: Noisy and prone to false positives — treat output as leads.

tools.name: masscan
tools.purpose: Asynchronous port scanner built for very large ranges — sweeps a whole network far faster than nmap, at the cost of detail.

templates.label: Fast sweep of a range
templates.note: Keep --rate conservative on networks you do not own; it is a flood by design.

templates.label: Top ports across a CIDR
templates.note: Feed the open ports into nmap -sCV for detail.

flags.what: packets per second (the whole point — and the risk)

tools.name: amass
tools.purpose: In-depth subdomain enumeration and attack-surface mapping, combining passive sources with active resolution.

templates.label: Passive enumeration
templates.note: No traffic to the target — safe first pass and usually in scope.

templates.label: Active enumeration
templates.note: Resolves and probes; confirm it is in scope first.

flags.what: OSINT sources only, no target traffic

tools.name: subfinder
tools.purpose: Fast passive subdomain discovery from many public sources. The usual first step of a bug-bounty recon chain.

templates.label: Passive subdomains
templates.note: Pipe into dnsx/httpx to keep only what resolves and answers.

templates.label: Subdomains, then live hosts
templates.note: The standard recon one-liner: discover, then probe.

tools.name: assetfinder
tools.purpose: Small, fast passive subdomain finder — useful alongside subfinder/amass because the source sets differ.

templates.label: Subdomains for a domain
templates.note: Union its output with subfinder's; neither is a superset.

tools.name: theHarvester
tools.purpose: OSINT collection of emails, names, subdomains and hosts from public search engines and data sources.

templates.label: Multi-source OSINT sweep
templates.note: Passive; feeds username lists for later credential testing.

templates.label: One source, quick pass
templates.note: crt.sh is certificate transparency — cheap and reliable.

tools.name: dnsx
tools.purpose: Fast DNS resolution and probing toolkit — filters a candidate subdomain list down to what actually resolves.

templates.label: Resolve a candidate list
templates.note: Turns a guess list into confirmed hosts before you touch them.

templates.label: Record types for a domain
templates.note: CNAMEs matter — a dangling one is a takeover candidate.

tools.name: httpx
tools.purpose: Probes a host list for live HTTP services and reports status, title, tech and TLS detail. The bridge from recon to web testing.

templates.label: Probe a host list
templates.note: The output is the real attack surface; everything else was a guess.

templates.label: Probe one target
templates.note: Redirects often reveal the real application host.

tools.name: ffuf
tools.purpose: Very fast HTTP fuzzer — content discovery, parameter and vhost fuzzing, and form/login brute force via the FUZZ keyword.

templates.label: Directory discovery
templates.note: Match on status; filter noise with -fs once you see the 404 size.

templates.label: Virtual-host discovery
templates.note: -fs must filter the default response size or everything matches.

templates.label: Parameter discovery
templates.note: Hidden parameters are a common IDOR/injection entry point.

templates.label: POST login brute force
templates.note: Authorized testing only — check lockout policy before running.

flags.what: filter by response size — the noise killer

tools.name: feroxbuster
tools.purpose: Recursive content discovery in Rust — fast, and recursion-first, so it maps a tree rather than one level.

templates.label: Recursive discovery
templates.note: -d bounds the recursion depth; unbounded recursion is very loud.

templates.label: With extensions
templates.note: .bak/.old often expose source or config.

tools.name: gobuster
tools.purpose: Directory, DNS, vhost and S3-bucket brute forcing. Simple and dependable for a first content sweep.

templates.label: Directory brute force
templates.note: Add -x for extensions once you know the stack.

templates.label: DNS subdomain brute force
templates.note: Complements passive enumeration with guessable names.

templates.label: Virtual-host brute force
templates.note: Finds sites that only answer to the right Host header.

flags.what: the mode — they take different arguments

tools.name: nuclei
tools.purpose: Template-driven vulnerability and misconfiguration scanner with a large community ruleset. Breadth-first triage of a known surface.

templates.label: Full template run
templates.note: Update templates first; results are leads to verify, not findings.

templates.label: Against a host list
templates.note: The standard post-httpx pass across a whole surface.

templates.label: One tag only
templates.note: Narrow by tag (cve, exposure, takeover, misconfig) to cut noise.

flags.what: run only templates with a tag

tools.name: nikto
tools.purpose: Classic web-server scanner for known-dangerous files, outdated versions and server misconfiguration.

templates.label: Standard scan
templates.note: Very loud and signature-heavy; expect it in every WAF log.

templates.label: HTTPS with tuning
templates.note: -Tuning limits the test classes and the runtime.

tools.name: sqlmap
tools.purpose: Automated SQL injection detection and exploitation across many DBMS and injection techniques.

templates.label: Test a parameter
templates.note: Start low; raising level/risk sends far more, far noisier payloads.

templates.label: From a saved request
templates.note: A saved request keeps auth headers/cookies intact — usually the reliable route.

templates.label: Enumerate a database
templates.note: Enumerate before dumping; dumping data may exceed your authorization.

flags.what: read the request from a file

tools.name: wpscan
tools.purpose: WordPress-specific scanner: core/plugin/theme versions, known vulnerabilities, and user enumeration.

templates.label: Enumerate plugins, themes, users
templates.note: vp/vt are the VULNERABLE plugins/themes only — much less noise.

templates.label: With the vulnerability API
templates.note: The token unlocks the vulnerability database; without it you get versions only.

flags.what: what to enumerate (vp, vt, u, ap, at)
password list for login brute force

tools.name: dalfox
tools.purpose: XSS scanner and parameter analyser — finds reflection points and verifies which are actually exploitable.

templates.label: Scan a URL
templates.note: Verifies reflection in a headless browser, so fewer false positives.

templates.label: Scan a URL list
templates.note: Pair with gau/waybackurls output for breadth.

tools.name: whatweb
tools.purpose: Web technology fingerprinting — server, framework, CMS, analytics and version hints from responses.

templates.label: Fingerprint a target
templates.note: -a 3 is aggressive; -a 1 is passive and quieter.

tools.name: netexec
tools.purpose: Swiss-army knife for SMB/WinRM/LDAP/MSSQL across a network — auth checks, share and user enumeration, and post-auth actions. The maintained successor to CrackMapExec.

templates.label: Unauthenticated SMB fingerprint
templates.note: Names the host, domain, OS and signing state before you have creds.

templates.label: Validate credentials
templates.note: [+] means valid; (Pwn3d!) means local admin.

templates.label: Password spray a user list
templates.note: ONE password across many users. Check lockout thresholds first.

templates.label: Enumerate shares
templates.note: READ on an unexpected share is a common foothold.

templates.label: Enumerate domain users
templates.note: Feeds kerbrute/hashcat later in the chain.

flags.what: keep going after the first hit (spraying)
authenticate with an NTLM hash instead of a password

tools.name: enum4linux-ng
tools.purpose: Rewritten SMB/NetBIOS enumeration — users, groups, shares, password policy and OS detail, with structured output.

templates.label: Full enumeration
templates.note: -A is everything; the password policy tells you if spraying is safe.

templates.label: Authenticated enumeration
templates.note: Credentials usually turn a thin null-session result into a full one.

tools.name: smbmap
tools.purpose: Enumerates SMB shares and, critically, the permissions on them — read/write access per share at a glance.

templates.label: Null-session share list
templates.note: Anonymous read on a share is a frequent initial foothold.

templates.label: Authenticated share list
templates.note: Shows READ/WRITE per share for that identity.

templates.label: Recursive listing of a share
templates.note: Look for config files and backups before anything else.

tools.name: kerbrute
tools.purpose: Kerberos pre-auth abuse: username enumeration and password spraying that do not generate normal logon failure events.

templates.label: Enumerate valid usernames
templates.note: Valid names come back without a failed-logon event on most configs.

templates.label: Password spray
templates.note: One password, many users. Read the lockout policy first — this locks accounts.

tools.name: hydra
tools.purpose: Online credential brute force across many protocols (SSH, FTP, SMB, RDP, HTTP forms, and more).

templates.label: SSH
templates.note: Keep -t low: SSH rate-limits and high concurrency just gets you dropped.

templates.label: HTTP POST form
templates.note: The F= string must match the real failure text or every attempt reads as success.

templates.label: SMB
templates.note: One password across users is spraying — mind the lockout policy.

flags.what: stop at the first valid pair

tools.name: ldapsearch
tools.purpose: Raw LDAP querying of a directory — the ground truth for AD objects, attributes and ACLs.

templates.label: Anonymous naming contexts
templates.note: The cheapest way to confirm LDAP and learn the base DN.

templates.label: Authenticated user dump
templates.note: -b takes the base DN, e.g. DC=corp,DC=local.

templates.label: Find Kerberoastable accounts
templates.note: Service accounts with an SPN are the Kerberoasting candidates.

tools.name: bloodhound-python
tools.purpose: Remote AD collector producing the graph BloodHound analyses — sessions, ACLs, group nesting and delegation paths.

templates.label: Full collection
templates.note: -c All includes session data; DCOnly is far quieter if that matters.

templates.label: DC-only collection
templates.note: Reads only from the DC — no host-by-host touching.

tools.name: hashcat
tools.purpose: GPU-accelerated password recovery across hundreds of hash types, with rule, mask and hybrid attack modes.

templates.label: Wordlist attack
templates.note: -m is the hash MODE (1000 NTLM, 13100 Kerberoast, 22000 WPA).

templates.label: Wordlist + rules
templates.note: Rules are usually worth more than a bigger wordlist.

templates.label: Mask attack
templates.note: For a known password pattern — much faster than brute force.

templates.label: Show cracked
templates.note: Reads the potfile; no cracking work is done.

tools.name: john
tools.purpose: Password cracker with a large family of *2john converters that turn files (SSH keys, ZIP, KeePass, PDF) into crackable hashes.

templates.label: Wordlist attack
templates.note: Add --rules to mutate the wordlist.

templates.label: Convert an SSH key, then crack
templates.note: The *2john family covers zip2john, keepass2john, pdf2john and more.

templates.label: Show cracked
templates.note: Reads the pot file; no work is done.

tools.name: prowler
tools.purpose: Cloud security posture assessment for AWS/Azure/GCP against CIS and many other compliance frameworks.

templates.label: Full AWS assessment
templates.note: Read-only against the account the credentials belong to.

templates.label: CIS benchmark only
templates.note: Narrower and much faster than the full check set.

templates.label: Azure assessment
templates.note: Uses your existing az CLI session.

tools.name: scoutsuite
tools.purpose: Multi-cloud auditing that collects configuration and renders a browsable HTML risk report.

templates.label: AWS audit
templates.note: Read-only collection; the report is a static HTML tree.

templates.label: Azure audit
templates.note: Uses the logged-in az CLI identity.

flags.what: where the HTML report is written

tools.name: trivy
tools.purpose: Scanner for container images, filesystems and IaC — known CVEs, misconfiguration and exposed secrets.

templates.label: Scan a container image
templates.note: Pulls the image and reads it — nothing is run from inside it.

templates.label: Scan a filesystem
templates.note: Static: dependency CVEs, hardcoded secrets and IaC issues in one pass.

templates.label: Scan IaC
templates.note: Terraform/CloudFormation/Kubernetes manifests.

tools.name: kube-hunter
tools.purpose: Kubernetes cluster weakness hunter — probes for exposed components and known cluster attack paths.

templates.label: Remote scan
templates.note: Probes from outside the cluster.

templates.label: Scan a CIDR
templates.note: Confirm the range is in scope — this sweeps a network.

templates.label: From inside a pod
templates.note: Shows what a compromised pod can reach — the lateral view.

tools.name: ghidra
tools.purpose: Full reverse-engineering suite with a decompiler — static analysis of binaries across many architectures.

templates.label: Headless analysis
templates.note: Static: the binary is disassembled and decompiled, never executed.

flags.what: binary to import into the project

tools.name: radare2
tools.purpose: Command-line reverse-engineering framework — disassembly, analysis, patching and debugging.

templates.label: Analyse and list functions
templates.note: Static analysis; -q exits after the command.

templates.label: Disassemble main
templates.note: pdf = print disassembly of a function.

templates.label: List strings
templates.note: izz covers the whole binary, not just the data section.

flags.what: debug mode (this one DOES run the binary)

tools.name: gdb
tools.purpose: The GNU debugger — dynamic analysis, crash triage and exploit development, usually with a plugin like pwndbg or GEF.

templates.label: Inspect functions without running
templates.note: -batch with info commands inspects the file; it does not run it.

templates.label: Check binary protections
templates.note: Needs pwndbg/GEF. NX/PIE/canary decide the exploitation route.

tools.name: strings
tools.purpose: Extracts printable strings from a binary — the cheapest first look for URLs, paths, keys and version markers.

templates.label: All strings
templates.note: -n 8 cuts most of the noise; purely static.

templates.label: Search for a marker
templates.note: Hardcoded hosts, keys and flags surface here first.
